solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Times writing about a festival

parts.note: the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: one thing written about another is wrapped around it, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Newspaper columnists produce pieces about some festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper, but it is the X of multiplication; MS (manuscript) goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated form names the Christian holiday on 25 December, a major annual celebration.

clue.text: Insect turning up, say, before dark

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, as in 'say'
dim means poorly lit

explanation.surface: A bug rises into the air just before nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts the first piece ahead of the second; then both are reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged fly, often biting, that swarms near water at dusk.

clue.text: Repulsive gang getting in the middle of police

indicators.note: something getting in goes inside the other piece, so one set of letters is placed within the other

parts.note: a squad is a group or gang

indicators.note: only the central letters of the following word are wanted, its ends discarded

parts.note: the two central letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A nasty gang infiltrates the heart of the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid describes something filthy and sordid, so it works as a near synonym for disgusting or repulsive.

clue.text: In shops, woman and daughter hold hands?

indicators.note: a container that holds something has it inside, so the shops go around the people

parts.note: stores are shops
the first woman in Genesis, a standard crossword woman
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Mother and daughter hold hands while out shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold hands' looks like an affectionate gesture, but 'hold' is the container and 'hands?' is the definition, the question mark flagging hands as workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are manual workers; stevedores are dock labourers who load and unload ships, a specific kind of hired hand.

clue.text: Brilliant appearance of sub, over in Tottenham, cut short

indicators.note: these letters go inside the shortened football nickname
cut short means the last letter of the club nickname is removed

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
in British English to sub someone is to lend them money
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A substitute's flashy performance, having come on at Tottenham, is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub' looks like a football substitute, matching Tottenham, but here it means lend, as in subbing a friend some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or grandeur, a dazzling, impressive look, so it matches a brilliant appearance.

clue.text: European heads, with coolness, finally admitted leaks

indicators.note: a letter admitted is let in, so it goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: standard abbreviation for European
a head or headland is a cape

indicators.note: finally keeps just the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of coolness

explanation.surface: Cool-headed European leaders let slip some confidential information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' suggests leaders, but it means headlands.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns, leaks and escapes both mean gas or liquid getting out through a gap, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Scratching insect makes mammal run off

indicators.note: scratching something means crossing it out, so those letters are struck from the longer word

parts.note: the antelope is a hoofed mammal
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An itchy bite from a bug sends some animal bolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching' reads as relieving an itch; here it means deleting the ant from the front of the mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually with a lover in order to marry.

clue.text: Removing the head destroys fresh seafood

indicators.note: fresh signals a new version, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taking the head off a word drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Decapitating something ruins good fresh seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the D of destroys, then reorder what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are edible bivalve shellfish, eaten raw or cooked, a classic example of seafood.

clue.text: Labour aim always to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means what counts is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: end is an aim and ever means always

explanation.surface: The Labour Party's constant ambition is to win a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party but is the ordinary noun for effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour and endeavour both mean strenuous effort or hard work directed at achieving something.

clue.text: Cheated and voted twice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: betrayed a partner after pretending to cooperate
second meaning, read literally: marked two crosses on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Someone committed electoral fraud by voting more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: A vote is marked with a cross, so voting twice leaves a double cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to betray someone you are supposedly working with, a form of cheating them.

clue.text: Film director needing an ending went overboard

indicators.note: a name needing an ending lacks its final letter

parts.note: Federico Fellini, the Italian film director

explanation.surface: A movie director needed a finale and took things too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went overboard' suggests excess, but the definition is literal: dropped over the side of a boat into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overboard from a ship means toppling into the sea, which is exactly to have dropped into the water.

clue.text: Design surrounding emblem is oddly vulgar

indicators.note: one piece surrounding another goes around it on both sides

parts.note: a plan is a design

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the first, third, fifth and further odd positions

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A design around some badge strikes one as strangely tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian means belonging to the common people, hence coarse, lowbrow or unrefined, which is one sense of vulgar.

clue.text: Academic rooms for recording university dons

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the rooms wear the letter like a garment around it

parts.note: recording studios
standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: College lecturers use the recording rooms at their university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university lecturers, fitting the academic scene, but it is a verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, academic and studious both describe someone devoted to study and scholarly learning.

clue.text: Trains carrying sixty-eight empty boxes

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to train is to teach

indicators.note: an emptied word loses everything between its first and last letters

parts.note: only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: Railway trains hauling sixty-eight empty containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' reads as railway carriages, but it is the verb meaning instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests are large wooden crates, once used to ship tea, now commonly for packing when moving house.

clue.text: It's lucky the old lady has somewhere to sleep

parts.note: the old lady is slang for one's mother
as in the contraction 's, short for has
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: How fortunate that the elderly woman has a bed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's lucky' reads as an exclamation, but it defines a thing believed to bring luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept as a charm because it is thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Mother cares awfully about sons being butchers

indicators.note: the first pieces sit about the other, wrapping around it

parts.note: an informal word for mother

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A mother frets terribly about her boys becoming butchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butchers' looks like a plural noun for the trade the sons enter, but it is a verb meaning slaughters.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to kill them brutally in large numbers, which is exactly what massacring them means.

clue.text: Agreed to a German weapon after it's cut a gemstone

indicators.note: the weapon has been cut, losing one letter, as stated by the trailing words

parts.note: ja is the German word for yes, which is how a German agrees
a spear is a weapon

explanation.surface: A German assented to a weapon after it had cut a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the shortened weapon behind the German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, usually reddish variety of chalcedony quartz, polished as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Old coin shop is to let, but not all of it

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies within a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: The old coin shop has a To Let sign up, but only part of the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistole was a gold coin used in Spain and elsewhere in Europe in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Girl this writer recalled in prayers

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rosary is a sequence of Catholic prayers

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: The writer remembered a girl when praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' seems to mean remembered, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a female given name, and crosswords often define any first name simply as girl.

clue.text: Very dry port overwhelms Italian food

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the port swallows the other letters

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port
so means very
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A very dry port wine overpowers an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' and 'port' suggest wine, but dry here means abstaining from drink and port is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a northern Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock until creamy.

clue.text: Good-looking girl is entertaining weirdos

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so these letters hold the others

parts.note: Ms is a title for a woman
taken as written
fit is British slang for attractive

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman hosts some oddballs.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfits are people who do not fit in socially, so they come across as odd or eccentric.

clue.text: With less fluid they sometimes contain peas

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed in shape, so the letters can flow into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pea pods sometimes hold peas, with less liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a referee's whistle traditionally has a little ball, the pea, rattling inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional pea whistle contains a small ball, called a pea, which vibrates to make the trilling sound.

clue.text: Tastes defeats

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tries with the tongue
second meaning: beats soundly, as in informal usage

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means running a tongue over food, and informally it also means thrashing an opponent.

clue.text: When to start to seek first aid

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of seek
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Instructions on when to begin looking for first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first aid' reads as one phrase, but first is wordplay and aid alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to help or support them, a straightforward synonym of aid.

clue.text: Ages used up wrapping Eastern garment

indicators.note: in a down entry, up tells us to read the letters from the bottom
wrapping something puts it inside, so the other letter goes within

parts.note: eras are ages
standard abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: Years spent wrapping oneself in an exotic eastern robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A saree is a long length of cloth draped around the body, worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Put an end to bank sheltering stray dog

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to put an end to it

indicators.note: a shelter holds something inside it, so these letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier
to err is to stray from what is right

explanation.surface: Stop the bank from taking in a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' looks like an adjective for the dog, but it is the verb meaning wander off course.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scotch terrier, or Scottie, is a small, wiry, short-legged breed of dog from Scotland.

clue.text: Like one separating people making spiteful remarks

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: something separating a group gets between its members, so it goes inside

parts.note: persons are people
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Like someone who drives people apart by making nasty comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspersions are damaging or disparaging claims about someone's character, as in casting aspersions.

clue.text: An Olympian retired somewhere in Egypt

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Zeus, king of the gods on Mount Olympus

explanation.surface: A former Olympic athlete has retired to live in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete, but it is one of the Greek gods of Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is an Egyptian port city, which gives its name to the canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
